div.div:
مُتَدَوِّمَاتٌ , applied to birds, means Going round, or circling, over a thing: and this is meant by ↓ مُتَدَاوِمَات , which is used for the former word, in the saying [of a rájiz], describing horses, “كَالطَّيْرِ تَبْقِى مُتَدَاوِمَاتِهَا
” i. e. Like birds when thou lookest at, or watchest, those of them that are going round, or circling, over a thing: (S, TA: *) or متدوّمات signifies waiting, or watching. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
